claims.statement: Vosilasarm is the World Health Organization International Nonproprietary Name (INN) assigned to the compound long known in gray-market/research-chemical and bodybuilding contexts as RAD-140 or 'Testolone'; it is not a structural analog of RAD-140 but the same molecule (PubChem CID 44200882, molecular formula C20H16ClN5O2), now also being developed clinically under the code name EP0062 by Ellipses Pharma for oncology use. Sources discussing 'RAD-140', 'Testolone', 'EP0062', and 'Vosilasarm' should be treated as referring to one compound unless a source states otherwise.

claims.statement: Vosilasarm/RAD-140 is a non-steroidal, orally bioavailable selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) that acts as an androgen receptor agonist; in the oncology development program this AR-agonist activity is being exploited because the androgen receptor can act as a tumor suppressor in AR+/ER+ breast cancer, distinct from the anabolic/myotropic rationale used in bodybuilding marketing of the same molecule.

extractedEvidence.quote: the AR acts as a tumour suppressor in multiple contexts of ER+ breast cancer
SHBG decreased in 18 per 18 patients, and PSA increased in 16 per 20 patients. Paired baseline and on-treatment tumor biopsies demonstrated AR engagement.

reviewFlags: mechanism evidence for AR-agonist tumor-suppressor activity is from an investigational oncology context and must not be read as evidence for anabolic/muscle-building claims

claims.statement: FDA has issued a warning letter identifying RAD-140/Testolone (marketed alongside other SARMs) as an unapproved 'new drug' under the FD&C Act when sold as a bodybuilding/research-chemical product for human use, citing violations of sections 301(d) and 505(a); no vosilasarm/RAD-140 product is FDA-approved for any indication as of this packet's generation date. The agency also states that SARM-containing products have been linked to life-threatening reactions.

context.population: consumers purchasing SARM products marketed as research chemicals or bodybuilding supplements

extractedEvidence.quote: "RAD-140 Testolone," "MK-677 Ibutamoren," "MK-2866 Ostarine," and "LGD-4033 Ligandrol" are classified as "new drugs" lacking FDA approval and violate sections 301(d) and 505(a) of the FD&C Act.
Life-threatening reactions, including liver toxicity, have occurred in people taking products containing SARMs. SARMs also have the potential to increase the risk of heart attack and stroke.

claims.statement: In the first-in-human Phase 1 dose-escalation study of RAD140/vosilasarm in 22 heavily pretreated ER+/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer patients (50/100/150 mg once daily), the maximum tolerated dose was 100 mg daily; clinical benefit rate at 24 weeks was 18.2% and median progression-free survival was 2.3 months, with only one confirmed partial response (in a patient with a baseline ESR1 mutation). This is a modest, early-phase oncology efficacy signal in a specific pretreated cancer population and must not be generalized to any performance, muscle-building, or general-health benefit claim.

claims.statement: Human evidence documents clinically significant, dose- and duration-limited hepatotoxicity with RAD-140/vosilasarm in both the oncology trial setting and gray-market bodybuilding use. In the Phase 1 oncology trial, treatment-related AST/ALT elevation occurred in 59.1%/45.5% of patients and Grade 3/4 AST/ALT elevation in 22.7%; separately, a published case report describes a man who developed severe cholestatic drug-induced liver injury (peak total bilirubin 708 micromol/L, reference <20) after two months of self-administered gray-market RAD-140 for bodybuilding, with biopsy-confirmed bland cholestatic hepatitis; liver biochemistry normalized within five months of discontinuation and monitoring.

context.population: oncology trial patients (supervised, dose-escalation) and a gray-market bodybuilding user (unsupervised, self-administered)
context.formulation: investigational oral RAD140/vosilasarm (trial) and unregulated gray-market RAD-140 product (case report)

conflicts.summary: Vosilasarm/RAD-140 has a modest, supervised, early-phase oncology efficacy and safety dataset in a specific pretreated AR+/ER+/HER2- breast cancer population, while online gray-market marketing extrapolates from the same molecule's AR-agonist mechanism to unsupported bodybuilding/anabolic benefit claims in an entirely different (healthy, self-administering) population; the oncology data cannot be used to validate the bodybuilding marketing claims, and no controlled human efficacy or long-term safety data exist for the bodybuilding use case.
